doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: Laid off after 21 years and never looking back
summary: She was laid off at 58 with a year's severance, then worked full time as a musician ever since.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: like so — how do they do this to me you know, after I worked here all these 21 years and oh my God and feeling sorry for myself and the whole trip. You know what? I had prayed that I would be able to start singing more. And be careful what you pray for, you might get it. And you know what? I never looked back. I have never looked back. I collected that money for one year, that salary, and I’ve been working ever since. And I’m doing more work now than I’ve ever done. Everybody says, “Aren’t you going to retire?” I say, “Retire from what?” Retire? That’s like telling me to go and dig a grave and jump in it. I’ll retire when I go under.
Yeah. Now you’re doing what you were meant to do.

Of course. I’m doing everything I want to do in my life today, it’s teaching, it’s talking to people like you and going out and doing concerts. I’m constantly working. You know I never though I’d have to turn down gigs, how about that?
